capacity_utilization.note: ISSUER STATES NIL - this is the RHP's own affirmative 'not applicable', NOT an extraction gap. Verbatim, under the heading 'CAPACITY AND CAPACITY UTILIZATION' in 'Our Business' (RHP printed page 205 / PDF page 209): 'Our Company is engaged in media and entertainment services and hence capacity and capacity utilization is not applicable to us.' Corroborated twice: under 'RAW MATERIALS' in the same chapter (printed page 203 / PDF page 207) - 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us.'; and under 'Capacity/facility creation, location of plants' in 'History and Certain Corporate Matters' (printed page 228 / PDF page 232) - 'Since our Company is engaged in M&E Industry, we do not have any product manufacturing facilities.' The RHP prints NO installed capacity, no studio / floor / screen capacity, no production-slate capacity (films or episodes per year) and no utilisation percentage anywhere, for any FY. Every other 'capacity' occurrence in the issuer's own sections was checked and none is a capacity disclosure: (i) the growth strategy 'Increase our production capacity' (printed page 198 / PDF page 202) is purely qualitative - 'we will expand our organization's sourcing and production capacity ... by hiring young talent, grooming them and building a creative leadership bench' - and attaches no number, no unit and no slate count; (ii) the Risk Factors mention (printed page 47 / PDF page 51) is about third-party exhibitors - 'there can be no assurance that occupancy rates at theatres in India or demand for our projects will not fall' - i.e. cinemas' occupancy, not the Company's capacity; (iii) the remaining hits are auditors/experts acting 'in their capacity as', a KMP acting 'in his capacity', and D&B industry-chapter text (pages 137, 146, 160) which is commissioned third-party material, not issuer disclosure. The Company owns no production facility: its only owned operating premises is an administrative office, and its other locations are a leased registered office and two leased storage godowns (see plants[]); equipment such as cameras, lights and grips is rented from third-party local players. Consequently installed_by_fy and utilization_pct_by_fy are correctly null - the issuer states the concept does not apply to it.

channel_mix.note: ISSUER-SILENT, verified - the RHP prints no B2B/B2C split and no distribution-channel revenue split of any kind, so b2b_pct / b2c_pct are correctly null. Search terms run over the full staged text (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed): 'B2B' 0 hits, 'B2C' 0 hits, 'business-to-business' 0, 'business to business' 0, 'business-to-consumer' 0, 'direct-to-consumer' 0, 'channel partner' 0, 'aggregator' 0; 'end consumer' 1 hit and 'syndication' 2 hits, all three in the commissioned D&B industry chapter or in the marketing narrative, none carrying a split; 'sub-distributor' 1 hit (box-office reporting risk factor). Also probed by the document's own phrasing - 'theatrical', 'theatrical rights', 'satellite rights', 'digital rights', 'music rights', 'distribution rights', 'overseas rights', 'revenue stream', 'revenue model', 'mode of exploitation', 'bifurcation', '% of total revenue', 'as % of revenue' - and no theatrical-vs-OTT-vs-satellite-vs-music revenue table exists for the issuer (the only theatrical/digital percentage split in the document, 61% domestic theatricals, is D&B industry data on PDF page 189 and is expressly excluded). What the RHP does say qualitatively about its routes to market, under 'OUR CUSTOMERS' (printed page 202 / PDF page 206): 'We generate a major portion of revenues from renowned studios with whom we co-produced our films and independent distributors whom we sell our distribution rights' - and elsewhere it names OTT platforms, broadcasters and its own social-media channels (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook) as monetisation routes, plus overseas distributors for export. The customer table on that page is a top-1/3/5/10 CONCENTRATION table (already in customer_concentration), not a channel split, and the RHP adds that it cannot name those customers for want of consent. The model is substantively 100% business-to-business (studios, distributors, OTT platforms, broadcasters and overseas distributors are the paying counterparties; theatrical receipts reach the Company as a share of gross box office collected through exhibitors and distributors), but the RHP never states a percentage, so no b2b_pct is recorded here rather than deriving one. NOTE ON WHAT IS NOT A CHANNEL MIX: revenue_split_product (films 89.68% / web-series 1.32% / others 8.99% for FY26) is a product-segment split, and the RHP's second table - sole-produced 90.00% vs co-produced 0.00% vs others 10.00% for FY26 (FY25: 78.60 / 21.38 / 0.02; FY24: 99.83 / 0.00 / 0.17, printed page 32 / PDF page 36) - is a production-model split; neither is a customer-type or distribution-channel mix. business_ops.seasonality: Stated not seasonal, verbatim: 'The extent to which business is seasonal. Our business does not depend to a certain extent on the seasonal, environmental and climate changes. Hence, our business is not seasonal in nature.' The RHP nonetheless lists among the factors that may affect future results: 'Revenues from theatrical releases are subject to volatility due to competition, seasonality, and audience turnout, which can fluctuate significantly.' Revenue is instead described as lumpy and release-driven - a major portion depends on the box office success of films and on streaming deals with OTT platforms, and MD&A explains the Fiscal 2026 inventory-days spike to 1,328 days (from 173 days in Fiscal 2025 and 119 days in Fiscal 2024) as a consequence of the Company having released only one major movie/web series during the year.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Vertically integrated content originator rather than a manufacturer: the Company states it engages in 'research & development of scripts, end-to-end production of content, intellectual property creation, monetization of rights and distribution'. Production runs from conceptualization and scripting, through cast/crew finalisation, a cost-of-production budget covering pre-production, production and post-production, and a separate Print and Advertising (P&A) budget covering marketing and distribution. Editing is generally carried out in-house 'for creative reasons'; dubbing, sound and VFX are outsourced to different studios/professionals while closely monitored. Post-production capability is described as digital intermediate (DI) colour grading, high-resolution editing suites, Dolby Atmos sound mixing and VFX pipelines. Two operating models: (i) co-production with a reputable studio, where the Company produces for a fixed fee plus a share of the intellectual property and profits, giving 'certainty in earnings' and de-risking cashflows; and (ii) sole production, where the Company finances the entire project and retains all rights - intellectual property, titles and distribution rights - allowing it to keep the entire theatrical upside and monetise OTT, music rights and downstream derivatives (remakes, sequels/prequels, spin-offs, dubbings, foreign-language renditions, stage plays, web series and television production). Forward channel is via renowned studios, independent distributors, OTT platforms and broadcasters, plus the Company's own social media presence (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook). Backward integration is deliberately light: 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us'; equipment (cameras, lights, grips, picture vehicles, setting equipment) is rented from third-party local players, while the Company uses its own editing equipment; power is drawn from the local grid supplemented by hired diesel generator sets at shooting sites; water is required only for drinking and sanitary purposes. Cost control measures include a no-cash / minimum-cash payment policy with payments through banking channels and on-set accountants to manage payments, track daily expenses and audit. The Company states it has not entered into any collaboration or joint venture 'except collaborating with other producers in the ordinary course of business on specific film projects'. Human resources: 28 full-time employees on roll as on June 2026 (Accounts and Finance 5, Admin 12, Business Development 8 including Executive Directors, IT 1, Compliance 1, HR 1), with approximately 150-300 skilled professionals and unskilled labour engaged per project over the production journey. Intellectual property is protected by copyright (registration optional in India) and by trademark applications: 'SUNSHINE PICTURES' application 6643047 (class 41) Accepted & Advertised, 6643048 (class 43) Abandoned, 6643049 (class 41) Objected, 6643050 (class 43) Abandoned, all applied September 26, 2024; and seven device-mark applications dated July 15, 2026 (7120962, 7120964, 7120967, 7120968, 7120969 - formalities check pass; 7120963, 7120965 - objected), all class 41. The Company also states it has no outstanding export obligations.

non_compliances.issue: Auditor's Emphasis of Matter in the examination report on the Restated Financial Statements: the assignment agreement with Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited dated March 27, 2026, transferring certain rights including delivery of tapes and materials and granting OTT release rights with effect from that date, was executed within the eight-week holdback period agreed with an exhibitor for the film 'The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond', whose first theatrical release was February 27, 2026. non_compliances.provision: Contractual minimum eight-week theatrical holdback with an exhibitor; raised as an auditor Emphasis of Matter, not as a statutory contravention
non_compliances.status: Management represents that the film was ultimately released on OTT on May 1, 2026, which falls after expiry of the stipulated eight-week holdback computed from the date of first theatrical release, so the arrangement was complied with in substance, and that no consequential legal implications have been identified. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter, and the RHP states the Restated Summary Statements do not contain any qualifications requiring adjustments.

non_compliances.issue: The restated balance sheet carries a liability line described as 'Liability for interest and late fees on TDS and income tax' of 48.24 lakhs as at March 31, 2026, 26.55 lakhs as at March 31, 2025 and 3.78 lakhs as at March 31, 2024. The RHP's risk factor on statutory dues separately states that the Company has made timely payment of goods and services tax (GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B), professional tax, employees' state insurance and employees' provident fund for the last three Fiscals and has not faced any such instances in the past.
non_compliances.provision: Income-tax Act, 1961 - interest and late fees on tax deducted at source and on income tax
non_compliances.status: Carried as a liability in the Restated Financial Statements for all three Fiscals presented and rising across them. opportunities: Expanding Market Dynamics (D&B SWOT): rising disposable income in India together with a growing number of cinema screens in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities; rapid growth of OTT platforms and increasing global appetite for diverse storytelling; rising international demand for Indian content.

Digital Media Transformation (D&B SWOT): India's high mobile penetration and affordable data plans drive content consumption, enabling mobile-first content strategies, interactive storytelling formats and use of audience data analytics.
Talent Development Ecosystem (D&B SWOT): fostering an attractive workplace for creative talent and building a robust internal talent pipeline to enhance long-term competitiveness.

Company-stated strategies: increase production capacity by expanding the writer pool and grooming young talent; diversify the portfolio across genres and formats, including the recently launched Sunshine Music and Sunshine Digital (Originals) verticals; strengthen the theatrical distribution business by acquiring films from other production houses.

Stated pipeline: six feature films and two web series under development, including co-production of "Hisaab" with Jio Studios and the film "Samuk" and web series "Nanavati vs Nanavati" for Amazon Seller Services Private Limited, all planned for release in Fiscal 2027 (subject to implementation based on available funds, market conditions and other factors).
strengths: Exceptional Leadership Ecosystem (D&B SWOT): led by Vipul Amrutlal Shah, whose 25+ years in filmmaking produced Aankhen, Namastey London, Singh Is Kinng, Waqt: The Race Against Time and London Dreams; Shefali Vipul Shah brings an Emmy nomination for Delhi Crime; Aryaman and Maurya Shah represent next-generation leadership under the Company's succession planning.

Innovative and Resilient Business Model (D&B SWOT): dual production strategy — standalone productions allow complete IP control and higher revenue potential while co-productions reduce financial risk through studio partnerships; cost management via profit-sharing agreements with actors, real-time budget monitoring and in-house story development; multiple revenue channels across theatrical, OTT rights, satellite rights, merchandising and music.

Comprehensive Industry Network (D&B SWOT): over 17 years of experience with relationships across top studios, talent agencies and creative professionals, and repeat collaborations with major industry players.
Intellectual Property Monetization Expertise (D&B SWOT): multiple revenue streams from sequels and adaptations, plus monetization of music rights.
Company-stated key strength — Experienced Promoters supported by senior management team.
Company-stated key strength — Established track record and long-standing relationships in the industry.

Company-stated key strength — Differentiated and robust business model; co-production fixed-fee arrangements give "assured revenues at every stage of completion of the film and a contractually assured minimum consideration, regardless of box-office outcomes", while retaining part IP share, profit share beyond a threshold and downstream OTT/television income.
Portfolio-level risk limit: exposure to any individual project capped at 30% of total annual budget.
Digital presence stated in the D&B Report: 167,000 YouTube subscribers and over 104.04 million views, and a combined Instagram and Facebook follower base of 120,000.
threats: Intense Competitive Landscape (D&B SWOT): competition from agile new entrants, international content providers and streaming platforms producing original content; rapidly changing audience preferences and shortened content consumption cycles.
Technological Disruption (D&B SWOT): emerging technologies such as AI and shifting content consumption patterns pose risks to traditional production methods, requiring continuous innovation.
Regulatory and Compliance Complexities (D&B SWOT): complex copyright enforcement, evolving content regulations and potential censorship risks, with compliance required across multiple territories.

Competition from dominant production houses named in the RHP — Yash Raj Films, Dharma Productions and Maddock Films Private Limited — which the RHP states maintain their edge through expansive portfolios, significant budgets and advanced production capabilities.
Sector-level challenges named in the RHP: heightened competition, regulatory changes, content saturation, piracy and IP protection issues.
Risk factor cited by the RHP: the Company may not be successful in adopting new digital distribution methods or may lose market share.
weaknesses: Inherent Volatility in Entertainment Production (D&B SWOT): high dependence on box office success, particularly for standalone productions; audience preferences are unpredictable and not all projects achieve the desired commercial outcomes, posing a risk of significant financial losses.

Limited Global Market Penetration (D&B SWOT): primarily focused on the Indian market with only a nascent international presence; global distribution networks remain underdeveloped and brand recognition outside India is relatively low.

Technological Adaptation Challenges (D&B SWOT): still in the early stages of adopting advanced technologies such as AR/VR; skill gaps and the need for continuous investment in technological infrastructure could limit its ability to compete with more tech-savvy competitors.

Scale relative to the disclosed peer set: Fiscal 2026 Total Income of ₹ 7,627.49 lakhs against ₹ 31,735.15 lakhs for Panorama Studios International and ₹ 22,116.73 lakhs for Balaji Telefilms, as printed in the RHP peer-comparison table.

The margin step-up sits in the inventory line, not in trading performance. Whether Fiscal 2026 margin is repeatable therefore depends entirely on how the ₹7,506.02 lakhs of capitalised content is ultimately monetised and expensed.

The three-year trend is not like-for-like. Fiscal 2026 is presented on a STANDALONE basis while Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024 are CONSOLIDATED — the statement headers, the cash-flow notes and the contingent-liability table all say so. The RHP's own KPI table compounds this: its column headers read 2026 (Standalone), 2025 (Consolidated), 2024 (Consolidated) while the note immediately below states that the financial figures for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 are based on consolidated financials. Every growth, margin and days comparison in the document, including the (27.96)% and (22.77)% revenue declines, crosses that basis change.

Working capital has swollen past the size of the business. Net working capital was ₹12,646.25 lakhs at March 31, 2026, stated as 169.89% of revenue from operations, against ₹7,298.19 lakhs (70.63%) at March 31, 2025 and ₹5,103.24 lakhs (38.14%) at March 31, 2024. Holding days printed by the Company: inventory 119 (Fiscal 2024), 173 (Fiscal 2025), 1,328 (Fiscal 2026); trade receivables 11, 64, 233; trade payables 29, 42, 34. Trade receivables of ₹6,650.54 lakhs and inventories of ₹7,506.02 lakhs at March 31, 2026 compare with revenue from operations of ₹7,443.67 lakhs for the same year. Management describes the 1,328 inventory days as purely a mathematical outcome of the formula and not slow-moving, obsolete or unsaleable stock.

The Fiscal 2027 working-capital plan assumes all three cycles reverse at once. The estimate takes trade receivables from 233 days to 117, inventory from 1,328 days to 314 and trade payables from 34 days to 11, with estimated inventories still rising to ₹18,304.31 lakhs and other current assets to ₹7,351.39 lakhs within a Total Working Capital Requirement of ₹32,049.37 lakhs. The reversal is stated to be contingent on the release and monetisation of Governor: The Silent Saviour (released June 12, 2026) and Hisaab (expected Q2 Fiscal 2027), and the estimate itself is stated to use assumptions about future events and management actions that are not necessarily expected to occur.

The only quantified object of the Fresh Issue is working capital of up to ₹11,250.00 lakhs, against the Company's own stated Fiscal 2027 requirement of ₹32,049.37 lakhs; General Corporate Purposes is printed as [●] and is capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds. The RHP states the deployment has not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, resting instead on management estimates of future financial performance approved by Board resolution dated July 27, 2026 and certified by the statutory auditor. There is no supplier, contract, purchase order or quotation behind any part of it — this is not a capex issue, so there is no execution schedule to test against.

The auditor's Emphasis of Matter goes to the timing of Fiscal 2026 revenue. The examination report records that the assignment agreement with Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited dated March 27, 2026, granting OTT release rights for The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond with effect from that date, was executed inside an eight-week theatrical holdback running from the first theatrical release of February 27, 2026, and was not in prima facie alignment with that holdback arrangement. The revenue was recognised in Fiscal 2025-26 under Ind AS 115. Management represents the OTT release actually occurred on May 1, 2026, after the holdback expired, and the auditor's opinion is not modified. The RHP prints no discrete amount for the transaction. The risk-factor chapter carries the matter as an orphaned paragraph at the end of RF 57, its heading missing.

The forward slate is named, dated and attached to identifiable counterparties rather than described generically: Hisaab, co-produced with Jio Studios, has completed principal photography and is in post-production for a Fiscal 2027 release; Nanavati vs Nanavati is a web series produced for Amazon Seller Services Private Limited with principal photography scheduled to commence July 20, 2026; Samuk is a sole production with photography scheduled from August 2026 and a Fiscal 2027 release; six films and two web series sit in the disclosed pipeline (Kaanha, Fevicol, Buldozer, Good Morning Rhea, Bheem, Maaya, Nanavati vs Nanavati Season 2 and The Kerala Story 3). Governor: The Silent Saviour was released June 12, 2026, after the Fiscal 2026 balance sheet date. The RHP attaches no value to any pipeline title.

The seventeen-year production record is quantified title by title, auditor-certified: Contribution to Company's Revenue (₹ in lakhs) The Kerala Story 14,704.18; Holiday: A Soldier is Never Off Duty 9,086.02; Bhed Bharam TV serial 4,950.00; Action Replayy 4,556.63; Humans web series 4,257.40; Sanak 4,143.35; The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond 3,970.85; Commando web series 2,803.34; Bastar 2,616.67; Force 2,446.56; Commando 2 2,368.45; Commando: One Man Army 1,613.28; Pukaar 1,575.00; Force 2 677.03; Commando 3 666.28; Bhai Bhaiya aur Brother 427.50; Kuch Love Jaisa 420.49; Happy Birthday Mummy Ji 30.00 (certified by M/s. Piyush Kothari & Associates, certificate dated July 27, 2026). Thirteen commercial films, two web series, three TV serials and one short film produced as on the date of the RHP.

Monitoring of the Fresh Issue is stronger than the regulatory minimum on one axis: CARE Ratings Limited (SEBI registration IN/CRA/004/1999) has been appointed as Monitoring Agency under a Monitoring Agency Agreement dated August 26, 2025, and the RHP states the mandate covers the Gross Proceeds, not merely the Net Proceeds, with quarterly reporting to the Audit Committee under Regulations 18(3) and 32(3) of the SEBI Listing Regulations and an annual statement of funds used for other purposes certified by the statutory auditor. The RHP also confirms no part of the Gross Proceeds will go to Promoters, Promoter Group, Directors, Group Companies or KMPs, and that Offer proceeds will not repay promoter loans.

The Bhed Bharam contract shows completed delivery rather than an open commitment: the RHP states all 150 contracted episodes were delivered and total revenue of ₹4,950.00 lakhs was billed to Prasar Bharati, Doordarshan, and that TRP performance will not affect the present contract. Export revenue rose to 13.45% of total revenue in Fiscal 2026 from 0.04% in Fiscal 2025 and 3.20% in Fiscal 2024.

The Board is eight strong with four Non-Executive Independent Directors, including Manmohan Ramanna Shetty (founder of Adlabs Films Limited, former Chairman of the National Film Development Corporation, over 31 years in the industry) and Kapil Bagla (over 21 years across financial services, investment banking and media). Audit and Nomination and Remuneration Committees were constituted September 30, 2024 and re-constituted April 24, 2026, with the Audit Committee chaired by a Chartered Accountant, Pawan S Bachani.

The stated co-production construct de-risks individual titles on the Company's own description: a fixed production fee with a contractually assured minimum consideration regardless of box-office outcome plus a share of intellectual property and profits beyond a threshold, and the D&B Report states exposure to any individual project is limited to 30% of the total annual budget. Contingent claims against the Company not acknowledged as debt are nil in all three fiscals and guarantees excluding financial guarantees are nil; total insurance coverage as of July 24, 2026 was ₹118,45,86,037, stated as 0.82 times the net assets of the Company.

Working capital funding for Fiscal 2027 is planned without new borrowing: the Sources of Finance rows print Borrowings for working capital requirements as nil, Total Equity/Internal Accruals ₹20,799.37 lakhs and Proceeds from the Offer ₹11,250.00 lakhs against a Total Working Capital Requirement of ₹32,049.37 lakhs. Historical borrowings in the same table fell from ₹1,666.82 lakhs (Fiscal 2024) to ₹849.73 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) to ₹691.16 lakhs (Fiscal 2026).

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Vertically integrated content originator rather than a manufacturer: the Company states it engages in 'research & development of scripts, end-to-end production of content, intellectual property creation, monetization of rights and distribution'. Production runs from conceptualization and scripting, through cast/crew finalisation, a cost-of-production budget covering pre-production, production and post-production, and a separate Print and Advertising (P&A) budget covering marketing and distribution. Editing is generally carried out in-house 'for creative reasons'; dubbing, sound and VFX are outsourced to different studios/professionals while closely monitored. Post-production capability is described as digital intermediate (DI) colour grading, high-resolution editing suites, Dolby Atmos sound mixing and VFX pipelines. Two operating models: (i) co-production with a reputable studio, where the Company produces for a fixed fee plus a share of the intellectual property and profits, giving 'certainty in earnings' and de-risking cashflows; and (ii) sole production, where the Company finances the entire project and retains all rights - intellectual property, titles and distribution rights - allowing it to keep the entire theatrical upside and monetise OTT, music rights and downstream derivatives (remakes, sequels/prequels, spin-offs, dubbings, foreign-language renditions, stage plays, web series and television production). Forward channel is via renowned studios, independent distributors, OTT platforms and broadcasters, plus the Company's own social media presence (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook). Backward integration is deliberately light: 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us'; equipment (cameras, lights, grips, picture vehicles, setting equipment) is rented from third-party local players, while the Company uses its own editing equipment; power is drawn from the local grid supplemented by hired diesel generator sets at shooting sites; water is required only for drinking and sanitary purposes. Cost control measures include a no-cash / minimum-cash payment policy with payments through banking channels and on-set accountants to manage payments, track daily expenses and audit. The Company states it has not entered into any collaboration or joint venture 'except collaborating with other producers in the ordinary course of business on specific film projects'. Human resources: 28 full-time employees on roll as on June 2026 (Accounts and Finance 5, Admin 12, Business Development 8 including Executive Directors, IT 1, Compliance 1, HR 1), with approximately 150-300 skilled professionals and unskilled labour engaged per project over the production journey. Intellectual property is protected by copyright (registration optional in India) and by trademark applications: 'SUNSHINE PICTURES' application 6643047 (class 41) Accepted & Advertised, 6643048 (class 43) Abandoned, 6643049 (class 41) Objected, 6643050 (class 43) Abandoned, all applied September 26, 2024; and seven device-mark applications dated July 15, 2026 (7120962, 7120964, 7120967, 7120968, 7120969 - formalities check pass; 7120963, 7120965 - objected), all class 41. The Company also states it has no outstanding export obligations.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Stated not seasonal, verbatim: 'The extent to which business is seasonal. Our business does not depend to a certain extent on the seasonal, environmental and climate changes. Hence, our business is not seasonal in nature.' The RHP nonetheless lists among the factors that may affect future results: 'Revenues from theatrical releases are subject to volatility due to competition, seasonality, and audience turnout, which can fluctuate significantly.' Revenue is instead described as lumpy and release-driven - a major portion depends on the box office success of films and on streaming deals with OTT platforms, and MD&A explains the Fiscal 2026 inventory-days spike to 1,328 days (from 173 days in Fiscal 2025 and 119 days in Fiscal 2024) as a consequence of the Company having released only one major movie/web series during the year.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- We derive the majority of our revenue from our top 5 customers i.e. the Studios and independent distributors.
- Any loss of these customers or loss of revenue from any of these customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.
- Note: Our top five customers i.e. studio and distributors may vary in the period indicated above. certificate dated July 27, 2026.
- The loss of one or more key customers for any reason, such as any inability to negotiate acceptable terms, contract renewals, disputes, adverse financial changes like bankruptcy of such customers, could negatively impact our business, operations, and financial condition.
- Any adverse developments our relationship with our customers could lead to significant revenue reductions from these customers, impacting our revenue, cash flow, and liquidity.
- While we have not faced any adverse situation with our customers during the last three Fiscals, we cannot assure that we will not face any such situation in future.
- Furthermore, these key studios/ independent distributors/ customers might choose to switch to competitors or decline to renew or enter into new agreements on favourable terms.
- We cannot guarantee that we will maintain historical business levels with our key customers or significantly reduce our customer concentration, both of which could affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
